title: A Novel $q$-Derivative Framework with Applications to $q$-Deformed Thermodynamics and Leakage Suppression in Superconducting Qubits
authors: André A. A. Marinho, Gisele B. Freitas, Clovis A. C. Filho
abstract: We propose a new $q$-derivative operator built directly from Jackson's $q$-number formulation, designed to preserve the structural properties of standard differential calculus while incorporating deformation effects. By analyzing $q$-deformed Heisenberg algebras, we demonstrate that this formulation maintains the consistency of thermodynamic quantities-such as internal energy, particle number, and specific heat-in dilute gas limits without requiring ad-hoc chain-rule modifications. Furthermore, we explore the physical implications of algebraic deformation using the Biedenharn-Macfarlane realization, showing how $q$-deformation induces intrinsic anharmonicity in quantum oscillator spectra and affects multi-level quantum systems ($d \ge 3$). Applying this algebraic scheme to superconducting transmon qubits, we derive analytical pulse-shaping corrections that generalize the Derivative Removal by Adiabatic Gate (DRAG) technique, offering a robust method to suppress computational leakage in ultra-fast quantum logic operations.
summary: This paper introduces a novel q-derivative framework to study physical systems under algebraic deformation. It applies this theory to derive corrections for superconducting qubits, offering a robust method to suppress computational leakage during fast quantum gates. Furthermore, it demonstrates the framework's utility in consistently describing q-deformed thermodynamic properties.
main_problem: The paper develops a novel q-derivative framework to model physical systems, specifically addressing q-deformed thermodynamics and suppressing computational leakage in superconducting qubits.
main_result: The framework successfully derives analytical pulse-shaping corrections for superconducting qubits, generalizing the DRAG technique to suppress leakage, while also showing that q-deformation induces intrinsic anharmonicity in quantum oscillator spectra.
method: The authors utilize a novel q-derivative operator built from Jackson's q-number formulation and apply it to analyze q-deformed Heisenberg algebras and superconducting qubit Hamiltonians.
model_or_system: The primary physical platform is superconducting transmon qubits, modeled in a three-level subspace. The theoretical framework involves q-deformed algebras, q-Fock spaces, and the application of the Biedenharn-Macfarlane realization.
key_observables: Leakage suppression fidelity ($F > 99.99\%$), $q$-deformed energy spectrum ($E_n$), internal energy ($U_q$), and specific heat ($C_V(q)$).
important_parameters: The deformation parameter $q$, the anharmonicity parameter $\delta_q$, and the gate time $T_{	ext{gate}}$ are crucial parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of the q-derivative framework to maintain structural consistency across different physical regimes, and it models the qubit dynamics within a three-level subspace.

paper_structure: The paper introduces the novel q-derivative, applies it to q-deformed thermodynamics (dilute gas limits), analyzes the resulting anharmonic spectra, and culminates in applying the formalism to derive pulse-shaping corrections for superconducting qubits.
why_interesting: It bridges abstract mathematical structures (q-calculus) with concrete, cutting-edge hardware challenges (superconducting qubit control), providing a generalized theoretical tool for error mitigation.
